open_questions.question: Who sets a spec's short tag: derived automatically from the title, written by the spec's author, or both (derived, then editable)? (Proposed: the author writes it, with a derived fallback.)

problem: The operator has to know a spec's name to filter by it. The scope picker (BoardScopePicker.tsx:23-71) lists specs alphabetically and matches typed text against long sentence-like titles. Meanwhile the board keeps accumulating finished tasks (322 tasks in this project on 2026-11-11), and a card does not say which spec it belongs to.

requirements.statement: The spec filter lists specs ordered by the most recent activity on any of their tasks (created or moved), newest first. 'All', 'Building' and 'No spec' stay at the top.
Each spec in the filter shows its short tag, how long ago its last task activity was ('2 h', '3 days'), and how many of its tasks are not finished.
Typing in the filter matches any spec whose short tag or title contains the typed text, case-insensitively, keeping the recency order.
Every spec has a short tag of at most 24 characters, unique within the project. Every card of a task belonging to a spec shows that tag.
By default the board shows no finished task. A task is finished when it is on main or closed without landing. The board states how many finished tasks it is hiding.
A 'show finished' switch on the board brings finished tasks back into view, marked as finished. The choice is remembered per project.

requirements.rationale: Looking up one old task should not require switching the whole board to show everything.
requirements.statement: The board's search also finds finished tasks while 'show finished' is off, showing them marked as finished.

in_scope: Ordering, labelling and searching the spec filter
A short tag per spec shown on cards
Hiding finished tasks with a switch to show them
non_goals: Deleting or archiving tasks from the database
Filters other than by spec (agent chips and search stay as they are, apart from search reaching finished tasks)

summary: The spec filter puts the specs with the most recent task activity first. Every card carries a short tag naming its spec. Tasks that are finished leave the default board, and a 'show finished' switch brings them back.

tasks.description: Acceptance drive first. Give specs a short tag, order the filter by last task activity, show tag, recency and unfinished count, and match search on tag or title.
